data.title: Where It Goes Next
data.text:
I am Mara Vey. I am in Carran, still adding to the archive. The Clachan power station went in an earlier thaw. In this last descent, the Upper Vell dam broke, and you reached the sea. The village lift and Tomas Lind's chalet remained standing. Lind kept kettles on every shelf; his chalet is one of the places the river passed without taking.

The land below is brown and grey now. The extraction, industry and energy you toppled earlier in Kessel, Power Valley, the Red Mesa and the Clachan made the damage worse. The choices there were not all alike. Calder Energy expanded its plant in Power Valley; the company brought jobs and cheap power, and more smoke. In Riverside, Anna Sorel proposed a spillway and flood wall. The Town Council put the work off, then funded a study instead of building it. Ruth Vey voted for the flood levy, and it failed. I have her kitchen calendar in the boxes, with four colours of pen.

I will not write you a pardon or a charge. You are the thaw coming down a valley whose choices were made over years. The next decision is still open: where the river goes next. You cannot undo the river behind you. You can still decide where it goes next.

In this last descent, the Upper Vell dam broke, and you reached the sea. The village lift and Tomas Lind's chalet remained standing. Tomas kept a kettle in every hut he used.

Here the rivers run brown, the sky is grey, and the grass is brown. The extraction, industry and energy you toppled earlier in Kessel, Power Valley, the Red Mesa and the Clachan made the damage worse. The choices there were not all alike. Calder Energy accepted a severe flood risk at Power Valley. The company put off moving its tanks and would not help pay for bigger spillways upstream. In Riverside, the flood levy vote failed in 2017. The national government paid for the flood wall, built in 2036 to the design first proposed in 2009. Ruth Vey voted for the levy, and it failed. Ruth ran her house by a kitchen calendar in four colours of pen.

I will not write you a pardon or a charge. You are the thaw coming down a valley whose choices were made over years. You cannot undo the river behind you. You can still decide where it goes next.

drafts.text:
I am Mara Vey. I am in Carran, still adding to the archive. The Clachan power station went in an earlier thaw. In this last descent, the Upper Vell dam broke, and you reached the sea. The village lift and Tomas Lind's chalet remained standing. Lind kept kettles on every shelf; his chalet is one of the places the river passed without taking.

The land below is brown and grey now. The extraction, industry and energy you toppled earlier in Kessel, Power Valley, the Red Mesa and the Clachan made the damage worse. The choices there were not all alike. Calder Energy expanded its plant in Power Valley; the company brought jobs and cheap power, and more smoke. In Riverside, Anna Sorel proposed a spillway and flood wall. The Town Council put the work off, then funded a study instead of building it. Ruth Vey voted for the flood levy, and it failed. I have her kitchen calendar in the boxes, with four colours of pen.

I will not write you a pardon or a charge. You are the thaw coming down a valley whose choices were made over years. The next decision is still open: where the river goes next. You cannot undo the river behind you. You can still decide where it goes next.
